title: Streak Snapped by 1.74: Zoe Stuns Team Pillbert as the Commish Drops 146.72
dek: Ghostu-Spider SZN ends Alan's five-game run by less than two points, The Horse is Hea posts the week's top score and nearly triples its title odds, and Week 8 hands us a Sonny-Alan rematch with every traded player on the field.
body: Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN beat Alan's Team Pillbert 87.96 to 86.22 as a 28% underdog, ending a five-game Team Pillbert winning streak by 1.74 points. Zoe did it the hard way, too: Nico Collins scored 1.6 on a 14.01 projection, the week's biggest bust. Alan had his own dud in Jalen Coker, who posted 1.4 on a 12.57 projection, more than 11 points short in a game decided by less than two. Javonte Williams did his part with 21.5, but Justin Jefferson (6.4) and Chuba Hubbard (8) didn't have enough between them to bail out Philly. The rookie is now 3-4, has won two of her last four, and has beaten both of the teams that sat at the top of the standings when she played them.

The best scoreboard of the week belonged to Sonny. The Horse is Hea beat Randy's The fumblers 146.72 to 108.52, the top score in the league by 26.88 points. Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 26.8 on a 16.25 projection, Bucky Irving added 23.5 on a 12.81 projection, and Jameson Williams, last week's waiver pickup, went for 23.6 on an 8.95 projection. The big trade with Alan finally paid off in the lineup, with Ollie Gordon II (16.8) and George Pickens (13.7) combining for 30.5 after both sat on the bench last week. The commish's title odds jumped from 11% to 28%, the biggest gain of anyone in the league.

Randy didn't play badly so much as he played the wrong team. 108.52 is a respectable number, and Caleb Williams gave The fumblers 22.12 on a 17.59 projection. But Derrick Henry scored 5.4 on a 17.37 projection, his second straight bust after last week's 4.5, and that's a hard hole to climb out of against a 146-point team. The fumblers have lost four straight, sit fifth at 3-4, and have 24% playoff odds.

Kaushal's Habibsters beat Mekhi's Dawgs 119.84 to 93.58 in a 50-50 game, and they did it while leaving the biggest bench score in the league on the pine. Tony Pollard, whom Habib picked up last week, scored 35 on a 12.92 projection and never made it into the lineup. It didn't matter, because Drake Maye threw for 27.44 on a 20.59 projection and the Habibsters won by 26.26. Two straight wins have Kaushal at 3-4, in fourth place on points, with title odds up from 6% to 15%. The two-time champ is speeding back into the picture, which is the only kind of speeding the scoreboard approves of.

Mekhi had his own bench problem: Tee Higgins scored 23.8 on a 11.62 projection while sitting, though even that swap wouldn't have covered a 26.26-point margin. Ashton Jeanty gave Dawgs 17.6 in the lineup, and Kai went shopping for a quarterback, adding Aaron Rodgers. Dawgs are 2-5 with 9% playoff odds, but they've scored 736 points, more than the 3-4 Ghostu-Spider SZN, so the record is harsher than the roster.

Ramon's No Banner only HULK handled Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 98 to 60.88 as an 85% favorite, and Brucie had Zay Flowers' 23.7 on the bench and didn't need it. The strange part: Jordan had the best individual performance in the entire league. Joe Burrow scored 28.88 on a 19.31 projection, and the rest of the lineup combined for 32. Isaiah Likely scored 2.2 and Denzel Boston 4.2, so JMoney, a man who is here for the numbers, got one great number and a lot of small ones. Counting or not Counting GV is 1-6 and has been officially eliminated from the playoff odds at 0%.

The HULK is 6-1 with 927.4 points, 73.8 ahead of The Horse is Hea, and still somehow watched its title odds drop from 50% to 37% after a comfortable win, because Sonny surged and Kaushal crept up behind. Below Ramon, The Horse is Hea and Team Pillbert are both 5-2, with title odds of 28% and 17% and playoff odds of 98% and 94%. Then comes a three-way pileup at 3-4: Habibsters (69% playoff odds), The fumblers (24%), and Ghostu-Spider SZN (6%). On the wire, Sonny made seven moves, including dropping Patrick Mahomes for Lamar Jackson, Bryce Young for C.J. Stroud, Cam Skattebo for Jordan Mason, and cutting Terry McLaurin for kicker Will Reichard. He also cut the 49ers D/ST a week after picking it up, swapping it for the Broncos D/ST, and Randy, during a 10-move cleanup that sent Darren Waller, Jordan Addison, Alec Pierce, and Kenny Gainwell packing, picked up the Bears D/ST that the commish dropped last week. Ramon added Brandon Aubrey, the kicker Randy cut a week ago, Zoe brought back Blake Corum for David Montgomery, Kaushal added Germie Bernard and Tre Tucker, and Jordan swapped Ladd McConkey for J.K. Dobbins.

Week 8 has the game of the season so far: Team Pillbert against The Horse is Hea, 5-2 versus 5-2, with Pickens and Gordon on one side and Hubbard and DeVonta Smith on the other, the full trade on the field at once. Habibsters and Ghostu-Spider SZN meet in a 3-4 versus 3-4 game where Kaushal can tighten his grip on the fourth seed and Zoe can turn her 6% into a real argument. Randy gets Jordan, the best chance yet to end a four-game skid, and the HULK hosts Dawgs, where Mekhi will try to start the right players against the best team in the league.

social.author: Ghostu-Spider SZN Fan Club
social.text: Nico Collins gave us 1.6. We still ended a five-game winning streak. By 1.74. Is the rookie still a rookie? Asking for Team Pillbert. Habibsters, you're next.

social.author: Horse is Hea Faithful
social.text: 146.72. JSN 26.8. Jameson Williams 23.6 on an 8.95 projection. Bucky 23.5. Pickens and Gordon finally in the lineup for 30.5. Title odds 11% to 28%. Team Pillbert, see you Sunday.

social.author: Coker Watch
social.text: Jalen Coker: 1.4 on a 12.57 projection. Loss margin: 1.74. I have done the math and I would like to undo it. Still 5-2. Commish, you're up.

social.author: Gridiron Gary
social.text: Kaushal left Tony Pollard's 35 points on the bench and still won by 26.26. That's not a mistake, that's a flex. Habibsters now 69% to make the playoffs. Two-time champs gonna champ.

social.author: BFL Waiver Insider
social.text: Sources: the Bears D/ST the commish cut last week has been adopted by Randy. Sources also say Ramon picked up Brandon Aubrey a week after Randy dropped him. The BFL wire is officially a recycling program.

social.author: Fumblers Forever
social.text: Caleb 22.12. Henry 5.4, again. Scored 108.52 and ran into a 146-point buzzsaw. Four straight. Jordan next week and we are taking that one personally.

social.author: The Numbers Desk
social.text: Joe Burrow: 28.88, best score in the league. Everyone else: 32 combined. Final: 60.88. We had the top performer of the week and lost by 37.12. That's a statistic.

social.author: Odds Goblin
social.text: The HULK won by 37.12 and its title odds fell from 50% to 37%. Sonny won and went from 11% to 28%. Winning is good. Watching the guy behind you score 146 is less good.

social.author: Dawgs Den
social.text: Tee Higgins 23.8 on the bench. Jeanty 17.6 in the lineup. Aaron Rodgers on the roster. 736 points, more than a 3-4 team. The HULK is next and we are bringing everything.

trade_watch.take: The first week went to Alan, but Week 7 swung it back: Gordon (16.8) and Pickens (13.7) put up 30.5 in Sonny's blowout win, while Hubbard managed 8 and Smith didn't start in Team Pillbert's 1.74-point loss. Alan still leads in lineup points 43.6 to 30.5, but the gap shrank from 35.6 to 13.1 in one Sunday, and both teams meet next week.

No flip coming here. Javonte Williams added 21.5 in Alan's lineup and is up to 75.5 since the trade, while Stefon Diggs didn't start and stays stuck at 6 lineup points for Randy, a gap that grew from 48 to 69.5.

Mekhi keeps pulling away: Jeanty's 17.6 pushed Dawgs' side to 65.6 lineup points against Jefferson's 22.2 for Alan, who scored 6.4 this week. The gap went from 32.2 to 43.4, though Dawgs are still 2-5 to Team Pillbert's 5-2.

Rough week for Jordan's return: Likely scored 2.2 and Boston 4.2 as starters, while Egbuka sat with zero lineup points since the trade. It's still JMoney's deal at 56.2 lineup points to none for Alan, but the shine is coming off.

bios.1: Sonny's team posted the week's top score at 146.72 and saw its title odds rocket from 11% to 28%. The commish reshaped his roster again with seven moves, including cutting Patrick Mahomes for Lamar Jackson. Now he gets Alan in a 5-2 showdown with all four traded players in the building.
bios.2: Randy's team has dropped four straight and sits fifth at 3-4 with 24% playoff odds. Caleb Williams delivered, Derrick Henry didn't again, and a 10-move cleanup brought in the Bears D/ST among others. Jordan is next, and this is the game to stop the slide.
bios.3: Jordan's team is 1-6 and out of the playoff picture at 0%, even after getting the league's top performance from Joe Burrow at 28.88. The rest of the lineup gave him 32 combined. J.K. Dobbins arrives, Randy's team is next, and spoiler season is officially open.
bios.4: Alan's five-game streak ended in a 1.74-point loss to Zoe, and his title odds slipped from 26% to 17%. At 5-2 with 94% playoff odds he's still in great shape, but Week 8 against The Horse is Hea will decide who's the real second-best team.
bios.5: Mekhi's team is 2-5 with 9% playoff odds even though its 736 points beat a 3-4 team. Tee Higgins' 23.8 on the bench and a 26.26-point loss hurt, and Aaron Rodgers is the newest addition. The league leader is next, so a statement win is on the table.
bios.6: Kaushal has won two straight and sits fourth at 3-4, with title odds up from 6% to 15% and playoff odds at 69%. He won by 26.26 this week with Tony Pollard's 35 on the bench, so the ceiling is high. A 3-4 showdown with Zoe is next.
bios.7: Ramon's team is 6-1, leads the league with 927.4 points, and just won by 37.12 while leaving Zay Flowers' 23.7 on the bench. The only thing that's cooled off is the title odds, down to 37% as the chase pack closes in. Dawgs come next, and the HULK is still the team to beat.
bios.8: Zoe beat Team Pillbert by 1.74 as a 28% underdog despite Nico Collins scoring 1.6, and she's now 3-4. Playoff odds are only 6%, but she's in the 3-4 logjam, and a win over Habibsters next week would make things very interesting.
